definition: High-level: Subverting autonomous AI agents by manipulating prompts or upstream integrations so the agent performs unauthorized data access or actions (non-actionable description).
advanced_ttp: Indirect prompt manipulation via compromised third-party integrations; emphasis on stealth and exfiltration through orchestration policies (descriptive only).
2026_trends: AI orchestration amplifies scale; defensive controls include strict payload validation, allowlists for agent actions, and telemetry on agent task execution.
unknown_factor: Supply-chain poisoning of agent orchestration policies or weights leading to long-duration, stealthy data leakage.
detection: Monitor agent API calls for anomalous endpoints or task patterns; log and review all third-party integration events.
mitigation: Enforce least-privilege for agent tokens, restrict integrations, validate inputs, and perform regular policy audits and canary tests.

definition: High-level: Real-time synthesis of audio/video biometric evidence to bypass liveness checks and social engineering defenses (non-actionable).
advanced_ttp: Real-time man-in-the-middle on video conferencing feeds to substitute a high-fidelity AI-generated avatar during verification calls (descriptive).
2026_trends: Generative models increase fidelity; defenders focus on multi-modal attestation, hardware-backed device attestation, and active challenge-response checks.
unknown_factor: Firmware-level compromise of camera or biometric sensors that report forged attestations to verification servers.
detection: Cross-verify biometric streams with device telemetry, watch for replay/timing artifacts, and correlate session metadata for inconsistencies.
mitigation: Adopt multi-factor, multi-modal verification (biometrics + device-bound attestations), implement liveness-challenges, and use hardware attestation where available.

definition: High-level: Techniques that attempt to blind or unhook EDR sensors at kernel (ring-0) level, often using vulnerable or legitimately signed drivers (descriptive).
advanced_ttp: Bring-Your-Own-Vulnerable-Driver (BYOVD) strategies where attackers leverage legitimate-signed but vulnerable drivers to alter kernel callbacks and evade detection.
2026_trends: Hardware-assisted protections and stricter driver signing policies are being adopted to reduce attack surface.
unknown_factor: Firmware or hypervisor-based hooks that can render endpoint protections blind at scale.
detection: Monitor kernel module loads, driver signing anomalies, and telemetry for unexpected callback registration or EDR outages.
mitigation: Enforce strict driver signing and code integrity, restrict driver installation privileges, and validate drivers against known-good inventories.

definition: High-level: Exploiting implementation flaws or side-channels in post-quantum cryptography (PQC) libraries before they reach maturity (defensive, non-actionable overview).
advanced_ttp: Targeting timing and side-channel leakage in early PQC implementations (e.g., Kyber variants) to degrade key secrecy while avoiding obvious failures.
2026_trends: Increased adoption of vetted PQC implementations, constant-time migration patterns, and hybrid handshakes becoming mainstream.
unknown_factor: Fault-injection or micro-architectural attacks that specifically target PQC primitives to induce recoverable leakage.
detection: Monitor handshake timing distributions, unexpected negotiation fallbacks, and discrepancies in PQC key lifecycles.
mitigation: Use vetted PQC libraries, enable constant-time operations, apply side-channel hardening, and adopt hybrid handshake strategies during migration.

definition: High-level: Abuse of long-lived OAuth tokens or forgotten third-party integrations to move sensitive data through legitimate API flows (defensive summary only).
advanced_ttp: Chaining compromised SaaS app tokens across services to pivot and exfiltrate data via authorized API calls while minimizing network anomalies.
2026_trends: Organizations are moving toward centralized token inventories, short-lived tokens, and fine-grained OAuth scopes to reduce risk.
unknown_factor: Token-delegation chains that cross organizational boundaries enabling stealthy data aggregation.
detection: Track anomalous API requests and unusual cross-service access patterns; maintain an integration inventory.
mitigation: Rotate tokens, enforce least-privilege scopes, maintain an integration inventory, and revoke unused third-party app tokens.

definition: Technique for mapping air-gapped or remote facilities by intercepting Starlink-to-Ground-Station telemetry to triangulate hidden server clusters.
advanced_ttp: Using software-defined radio (SDR) to passively monitor 12GHz Starlink beacon signatures, correlating latency drops with physical hardware density.
emerging_trend_2026: AI-automated 'Constellation OSINT' where botnets scrape orbital satellite schedules to predict windows of target visibility.
the_unknown_factor: Identity-Forge: Creating high-fidelity digital replicas of satellite maintenance staff to gain legitimate terminal access to global mesh backbones.

definition: The use of real-time AI audio/video synthesis to impersonate executives during high-stakes 'Vibe-Coding' (AI-assisted dev) sessions.
advanced_ttp: Interception of Slack Huddle streams to inject malicious 'code-snippets' into the AI's generation buffer, which are then accepted by the developer as 'AI-generated'.
emerging_trend_2026: MFA-Fatigue v2.0: Triggering 'Zero-Click' push notifications via smart-wearable vulnerabilities (Apple Watch/Oura) that auto-approve due to high-stress biometric triggers.
the_unknown_factor: Neural Hijacking: Using ultrasonic audio frequencies in phishing calls to subtly influence a target's cognitive state toward compliance (Speculative/Proprietary).

definition: Using Machine-to-Machine (M2M) protocol flaws to unhook EDR/XDR agents before they can report to the cloud controller.
advanced_ttp: Exploiting 'Follina-2.0' (2026 Zero-Day) to drop a signed, vulnerable kernel driver (BYOVD) that strips the security suite's Process-Notify-Callbacks.
emerging_trend_2026: Cloud-Native Persistence: Living-off-the-Cloud (LotC) by creating 'Hidden Shadow Tenants' in Azure/AWS that monitor the legitimate admin's every move.
the_unknown_factor: Decentralized C2 (dC2): Using blockchain-based smart contracts as an immutable, un-killable C2 instruction set that defenders cannot block without crashing the network.

definition: Hiding exfiltrated data within the 'weights' or 'token-streams' of legitimate LLM queries to bypass Deep Packet Inspection (DPI).
advanced_ttp: Splitting sensitive data into micro-packets hidden inside innocuous-looking GPT-5 prompts, reconstructed at a remote 'Neural-Listener'.
emerging_trend_2026: Logic-Bomb Triggers: Encrypting the payload with the target's own public AI model weights, ensuring it only 'unlocks' when inside the target network.
the_unknown_factor: Supply-Chain Poisoning of AI Weights: Altering the global weights of a common open-source model (Llama-4) so it contains a backdoor for anyone using it.
